name: Marquee Companion [✓]
description:
Adds four independent capabilities: server-side filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), plus opt-in global recent-podcast discovery via Podcast Index using administrator-provided credentials, plus opt-in passwordless sign-in by emailed magic link over administrator-configured SMTP, plus an opt-in scheduled task that recovers the release date of items that arrived without one by reading it from the file name. The filtering API exposes a paginated, BaseItemDto-compatible endpoint and a capability endpoint for client feature-detection.

versions.changelog:
- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.
- Adds the seamless Marquee Companion panel to Jellyfin Web without manual web-client changes. - Adds paired Jellyfin 10/.NET 9 and Jellyfin 12/.NET 10 package builds.

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

Fix delayed SponsorBlock loading. Register the daily refresh scheduled task so Pending items are retried automatically, correct the 24-hour playback retry condition, and wait for playback-start processing so freshly fetched segments can reach the first playback session.

Actually fix segments not reaching clients. Jellyfin's IMediaSegmentManager.CreateSegmentAsync expects the second arg to be the MD5-derived provider id (new Guid(MD5(name.ToLowerInvariant() UTF-16 LE)).ToString("N")), not the literal provider name. We were passing "SponsorBlock" verbatim, so stored segments didn't match any registered provider and the public MediaSegments API filtered them out. Pre-compute the hash and pass that. After upgrading, hit Reset on the config page so old segments get re-fetched under the correct provider id.

Fix segments not reaching clients. v1.1.0.0 dropped the IMediaSegmentProvider registration to avoid the slow scan, but Jellyfin filters segments by registered provider, so stored segments were never served. Re-register a stub provider (Supports => false, GetMediaSegments => empty) so Jellyfin recognizes 'SponsorBlock' as a known provider while the orchestrator stays in charge of fetching.

Add admin Reset button on the plugin config page that wipes SponsorBlock state and owned segments for items in the configured library scope, so the orchestrator re-fetches on next playback. Useful for re-fetching items whose SponsorBlock data became available after the initial scan.

Replace media-segment scan with event-driven orchestrator. Add daily refresh task at configurable hour. Add per-library scoping (empty by default — admin must opt in). SQLite per-item state machine (Pending/HasData/NoData) with 48h sanity check.
Remove non-functional user segment actions table from config page.
Initial release.

name: ShareLinks
description:
Adds secure, expiring guest-share links for Jellyfin items using temporary hidden users, one-use token redemption, restrictive policies, and scheduled cleanup.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 08:14 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks
overview: Temporary guest links for Jellyfin movies and episodes.

versions.changelog: Fixes share links on Jellyfin 12 and the ShareLink button missing on new Docker installs.

Fixes redemption on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and later (#19). Jellyfin changed the signature of the method the plugin uses to set a guest's password, so every link failed with a MissingMethodException and the guest landed on the dead-link page. The plugin now picks whichever version of that method the server has, so the same build works on every 10.11 release. Tested on 10.11.8 and 10.11.11.

Guests are now blocked from other plugins' API endpoints on the server, not just hidden from their UI in the browser. A share guest holds a real Jellyfin token, so anything that only hid a button left the endpoint answering it. Jellyfin's own API is untouched: the share tag already limits it to the shared title, and playback needs it. The config page lists your installed plugins with a checkbox each, so you can let one through when it genuinely needs to serve guests, such as an intro skipper. The guest hidden selectors setting is renamed to say what it is: cosmetic, it tidies the view and enforces nothing. Also fixes the dashboard devices page coming up empty after a share expired: deleting a guest left its device row behind, and a device whose user is missing makes Jellyfin fail the whole device listing rather than skip one row.

Fixes a season share exposing the rest of the series: the tag was going onto the season's parent series, and Jellyfin treats a parent's tags as belonging to all of its children, so every other season became visible to the guest. Tagging now only ever goes downwards. Take this update if you have shared a season with a link that is still live. Also in this release: a link can be made multi-use from the create popup so several people can use it until it expires, with a configurable ceiling on how many watch at once (ten by default), and the dashboard gains a "Clean up finished links" button that removes revoked, expired and failed records.

The ShareLink button now sits in its own section at the bottom of the item menu, and only appears for a movie, series, season or episode instead of turning up on things like a cast member. It is properly admin only again: the current user was cached for the whole page, so switching accounts in the same tab could leave the button visible to a normal user (the server always refused them). Share tags are hidden from everyone except admins, on the title and in the tag filter. Security: one-use links can no longer be redeemed twice, the configured maximum expiry is respected, the raw token is dropped from storage when a link dies, the token secret file is 0600, guest accounts can no longer sign in from the login page at all, and the runtime reflection shims around Jellyfin's APIs are gone.

Series and seasons can now be shared, not just single movies and episodes: the share tags the whole tree so the guest can browse and play everything inside it, and cleanup strips it all again. Expired or invalid links now show a friendly page that redirects to the Jellyfin home instead of raw JSON. The guest hidden selectors setting now defaults to empty.

ShareLink button on the item menu, temporary guest users confined by tag policy, expiring links with a date/time picker, admin dashboard with revoke, and a configurable guest lockdown that hides tag/genre/studio/cast links, the add-to-playlist and add-to-collection actions, and other plugins' UI. The creation popup is localized in English and French. Guest sessions are now minted server side: no password is ever stored or sent anywhere, the guest page only carries a session token, and expired guests are cleaned up every 30 minutes.

name: Native Trickplay
description:
Generates HLS I-frame variants so Apple TV / AVPlayer clients get native
scrubbing thumbnails on the transport bar — no client-side overlay needed.
One-time ffmpeg cost per item, then cached.
Includes a configurable daily prune scheduled task (orphan removal,
age-based eviction, optional LRU size cap) so the cache doesn't grow
unbounded.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 08:14 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HarshLabs/jellyfin-plugin-native-trickplay/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/HarshLabs/jellyfin-plugin-native-trickplay
overview: Native HLS trickplay for AVPlayer-based clients (Apple TV).

versions.changelog: Videos whose HEVC stream declares a level above 5.0 (common with certain x265 encodes) were rejected by the Apple TV when served through the trickplay-enabled playlist, and the player fell back to the thumbnail track. The playlist now also offers a level 5.0 entry, the same approach Jellyfin uses for its own playlists, so these videos play normally with scrubbing thumbnails intact. No change for other videos.

- Fixed: trickplay playlists and image segments now enforce each user's library access and parental controls. Previously, any signed-in user could request the scrubbing thumbnails of items outside their allowed libraries.
- Improved: the dashboard's item list loads dramatically faster on large libraries (it no longer reads every cached playlist from disk just to show cache status).
- Improved: changing "Concurrent encodes" now takes effect immediately — no server restart needed.
- Fixed: corrupt video files could make HDR detection time out, producing washed-out thumbnails for HDR content.
- Fixed: searching with an extremely large season or episode number could error the item list.
- Hardened the release pipeline: build steps are now pinned to exact, immutable versions.

After updating, restart your server once as usual. No cache regeneration is required.

If you reinstall Jellyfin (or its database gets rebuilt) and point the plugin back at your existing cache folder, the plugin now relinks every cached entry to your library automatically — no re-encoding, no lost cache.

- New: orphaned cache entries (from a reinstall or database rebuild) are automatically relinked to your items at server startup and before every scheduled prune run.
- New: the dashboard shows a warning banner with a one-click "Relink orphaned entries" button whenever orphaned entries are detected.
- Fixed: Cache Status no longer counts orphaned entries as cached (previously it could show 100% coverage while every item listed as "not cached" and playback re-encoded).
- Fixed: the daily prune task no longer deletes a reinstalled server's still-valid cache — it relinks first and only removes entries that truly match nothing.

Update, restart your server once, and your cache reconnects on its own within about 30 seconds — or press the new Relink button on the plugin dashboard.

Fixes playback stalling on Apple TV when audio is passed through unchanged (stream copy). The playlist could advertise the wrong audio format, which made the player wait forever for audio it was never going to get. If playback ever froze right after turning subtitles off, this is that fix.
Fixed playback breaking on SDR variable-bitrate files when trickplay is enabled. Affected videos could freeze mid-playback or get stuck on a loading screen when resumed; they now play normally.

* On HDR sources, tone mapping now runs on the GPU when your ffmpeg build supports it (OpenCL for Intel QSV / VAAPI / AMD on Linux, CUDA for NVIDIA, Metal on macOS). The previous CPU tone-mapping path was the dominant cost on HDR content — moving it to the GPU is the bulk of the speedup. Falls back to the old CPU path automatically when no GPU tone-mapping filter is available.

* The ffmpeg filter chain now thins frames down to the trickplay rate (one every couple of seconds) before any per-frame work runs. Previously every decoded frame was transferred GPU → CPU before being discarded — for a 2-hour 4K HDR source that's hundreds of thousands of wasted full-resolution transfers.

* New "GPU tone-mapping for HDR" toggle in the plugin settings, on by default. Disable it if GPU tone-mapping misbehaves on your hardware — encodes still benefit from the filter-chain reorder.

* Encodes that hit a GPU tone-mapping issue now fall back to CPU tone-mapping automatically (keeping hardware decode), and only drop to full software decode if the hardware decoder itself fails. The dashboard's hardware-path column shows what's actually in use (e.g. "QSV+OCL", "VideoToolbox+VT") so you can see the path each encode is taking.

A user on an Intel iGPU reported that a 2-hour 4K HDR film took ~90 minutes to generate on the prior version. The same encode finishes in roughly 10 minutes on this version.

Previously, if you deleted a library from Jellyfin, the plugin's
"Find & select items" list and the daily pre-generation task kept
seeing items from the removed library until Jellyfin's next library
scan cleaned them up — which meant inflated totals on the dashboard
and the nightly task wasting time encoding files that were no longer
in any library.

The plugin now scopes its lookups to the libraries currently visible
in Jellyfin, so the moment you remove a library the dashboard total
matches the Cache Status widget and the pre-gen task stops touching
those items.

No action required — just update the plugin and the next dashboard
load will reflect the correct counts.

Avoids advertising an iframe trickplay variant whose playlist resolves
to a valid-but-empty stub on cache miss — that combination can stall
AVPlayer on tvOS 26 with seek-shifted on-demand transcodes. Trickplay
appears on the next playback session once the warmup task generates
the cache.

* Search results above 200 items now load progressively. Default page is 500; 'Load more' appends the next batch and 'Load all' pulls everything matching the current filter.
* New 'Select all N items matching this filter' link appears once you've checked some visible items in a paginated result. Click it to select every match — including items not yet rendered. The bulk Generate or Evict action then operates on the entire match set, not just the page in front of you.
* Selection persists across pagination — checking an item on page 1 stays checked when you load page 2.
* 'Clear selection' link in the banner dismisses an all-matching selection. Filter, sort, or search changes also reset selection automatically.

Cancel active encodings

* New "Cancel" button on each in-flight row in the Encoding-in-progress panel, plus a "Cancel all" button in the footer.
* Works for both queued items (waiting for an encoder slot) and items currently being encoded.
* Existing cached trickplay for the canceled item is preserved — only the in-progress attempt is dropped.
* Cancel is idempotent — a second click is harmless.

Release notes now reflect actual changes per release. Prior versions all showed "Initial release" due to a publishing oversight.

versions.changelog: Corretto il doppio caricamento dopo un aggiornamento (issue #2): lo ZIP contiene un meta.json con il nome del plugin, così Jellyfin tiene tutte le versioni sotto lo stesso nome e rimuove la vecchia, e all'avvio il plugin segna come superate le proprie copie più vecchie. AniList come fonte senza chiave insieme a TMDB: cast giapponese con i personaggi, studio di animazione, date, stato, voto, trailer, copertina e banner, solo nei campi vuoti. L'anno di una stagione senza date arriva dalla catena dei sequel di AniList, se gli episodi coincidono. Gli ID AniList che non corrispondono per tipo o anno vengono ignorati. Nuovo passo AniList nel setup. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Comunità per tutti: dopo una correzione il plugin chiede se condividerla e la invia tramite il servizio della comunità, senza account; il token GitHub diventa facoltativo. Si condividono anche le stagioni con una scheda propria, applicate agli altri solo se numero di stagione ed episodi coincidono. Elenco approvato aggiornato ogni giorno, controlli automatici e approvazione con un'etichetta, tessera Comunità in Inizio, passo Comunità nel setup e scelta della stagione in «Correggi un abbinamento». Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Pagina del plugin rifatta da zero con l'identità di AnimeClick: setup guidato al primo avvio e solo i passi nuovi dopo gli aggiornamenti importanti, vetrina degli ultimi anime aggiornati, cruscotto della collezione, libreria a locandine con titoli e trame uniti per anime, attivazione delle librerie a un clic e ricerca della scheda su AnimeClick per correggere un abbinamento. Corretti i conteggi dell'analisi di una singola serie, lo stato della condivisione comunitaria appena attivata e «Da verificare», che ora coincide con quanto «Sistema tutti i titoli» ricontrolla. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Scarta i titoli alternativi di un'altra stagione verificando il titolo inglese originale. Quando manca una fonte coerente, traduce il titolo inglese già valido; esclude i nomi dei file. Correzione trovata sul NAS in anteprima, senza salvare la proposta errata. Include le novità 1.2.1. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick come unico provider remoto per le librerie anime: identificazione TMDB verificata, completamento dei metadati senza altri plugin e immagini integrate Fanart → TMDB → AnimeClick. Chiavi Fanart personale e di progetto nelle impostazioni, con link e verifica. Numerazione, campi bloccati e immagini esistenti conservati. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick primo campo per campo: i valori generici lasciano spazio alle fonti configurate. Recupero italiano e traduzione dall’inglese anche per serie, film, generi e tag, senza mescolare titolo e trama. Le immagini conservano la precedenza dei provider ad alta risoluzione; nessun aggiornamento immagini o riparazione viene avviato dall’installazione. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Verifica degli ID esterni, conservazione dei titoli compilati e indicazione della fonte nell’avanzamento. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

La tua libreria con analisi automatica, viste separate, avanzamento reale e interruzione dei lavori. Recupero dei soli titoli mancanti con protezione dei metadati esistenti. Abbinamenti della comunità e invio automatico delle correzioni su GitHub, entrambi facoltativi e disattivati di default. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Major per Jellyfin 12 e .NET 10, verificata su 12.0 e 12.1. Interfaccia riprogettata con guida iniziale, preferenze semplici e strumenti avanzati separati. Identificazione automatica più prudente fra titoli simili, remake e stagioni; correzione manuale cercando il titolo in libreria e incollando il link AnimeClick, senza cancellazione diretta delle immagini. Corretti redirect di rete, collisioni e scadenza della cache, concorrenza nei refresh, rate limit e coerenza della coda traduzioni. AI opzionale e disattivabile senza perdere il profilo; impostazioni e credenziali esistenti conservate. 210 test backend per versione server e 11 test browser. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo: non installare su 10.11; le release precedenti restano disponibili. Dettagli e limiti delle verifiche nel rapporto di audit della release.

versions.changelog: v1.4.1.0: Replaces the generic comet mark with an original anime mascot across every plugin page, the item action, Jellyfin's dashboard sidebar, GitHub and the plugin catalog. Rewrites the README around installation, first-time setup and everyday workflows, and corrects outdated interface-language and YouTube extractor requirements. Release build with no warnings, 221 unit tests and 14 browser and accessibility tests. No breaking changes.

v1.4.0.0: YouTube import no longer needs anything installed. The extractor now travels inside the plugin package, so pasting a link works on a stock Jellyfin server; previously the feature reported that yt-dlp was missing and did nothing until somebody installed it by hand inside the container, where it also disappeared on the next container update. yt-dlp is still supported and is still preferred automatically when present, with no configuration, because it tracks YouTube's changes continuously while a bundled copy only moves when this plugin is released; neither is required, and the settings page reports which of the two is in use. Video is assembled from a container-matched video and audio pair rather than taken from one of YouTube's pre-muxed streams, which top out at 360p; the join is a stream copy, so it costs no re-encode, measured against real YouTube at 1080p VP9 plus Opus with 0.9s to download and 5.2s to join. Packaging note: the archive now contains four assemblies instead of one — the plugin plus YoutubeExplode, AngleSharp and JsonExtensions. Install through the plugin catalog as usual, Jellyfin unpacks all of them. The archive is packed from an explicit list rather than from the build output folder, which also holds around thirty Jellyfin and Microsoft.Extensions assemblies that must not ship, and the build fails if that set ever changes. Release build with no warnings, 220 unit tests and 14 browser tests. No breaking changes.

v1.2.0.0: The YouTube import introduced in 1.1.0.0 had only been verified with unit tests, a mocked interface and a successful build. Running it against real yt-dlp and ffmpeg surfaced three problems, one of them serious: the video path forced the webm container, so every source YouTube serves as H.264 was re-encoded to VP9 before it could be written. Measured on four cores at roughly a quarter of realtime: 76 seconds for a 20-second 1080p clip, which is about 13 minutes of pegged CPU for a single three-and-a-half-minute theme, and worse on NAS hardware. Jellyfin accepts any video it can recognise inside backdrops, so the webm constraint was never its own; it came from animethemes.moe having been the only source. The source container is now carried through and the stream simply copied, and the same video takes 7 seconds. Also fixed: a theme video with no video track is rejected instead of being written as a silent, picture-less backdrop, and theme videos are recognised in both webm and mp4 everywhere, including the link repair that registers them with Jellyfin (an imported mp4 previously existed on disk and never played). Configuration: ten places mutated the shared object without synchronization, so two dashboard actions at the same time could lose one of the two entries or fail part-way through writing the file; they all go through a single lock now. Seasons: a later season is no longer confidently given an earlier season's themes, because the group number was a position over episode ranges rather than a season the source declared, and a miss fell back to the first group; ordinals are now trusted only when the ranges divide the run cleanly, and otherwise all themes are offered. A single-season show no longer gets the same opening written twice, into both the series folder and the season folder. Growth and contention: the skip list, the manual bindings, the resolution cache and the unresolved list were all unbounded, and cache entries expired only if something queried that exact key again; all of them are capped now and the cache is swept on a schedule, and reads of the two stores no longer block a thread each. Also: stale theme references are removed instead of accumulating, a malformed library pattern can no longer hang a sync, the playlist is written atomically and removed when empty, ffmpeg runs are capped plugin-wide (the previous limit applied only within a single request), and the choice of the root theme.mp3 is deterministic. 213 unit tests and 15 interface and accessibility tests. No breaking changes.

v1.3.1.0: The Theme Finder no longer shows a message about yt-dlp. Opening it on a server without the extractor produced an error-styled panel reading "yt-dlp was not found. Install it in the Jellyfin environment, or set its full path in the plugin settings.", in the middle of the page you opened to add a theme; an install instruction for a command-line tool is not an answer to that intent, and it made a feature that was never enabled look broken. When YouTube import is turned off, or the extractor is not installed, the import card is simply not shown. Whether the extractor was found, and where it was searched for, is still reported on the plugin settings page, directly below the YouTube import toggle and the yt-dlp path field, which is where it is actionable. Release build with no warnings, 213 unit tests and 13 browser tests; two new tests assert the card is absent, one for a missing extractor and one for the feature being off, and check that the string yt-dlp appears nowhere in the page. No breaking changes.

v1.3.0.0: The plugin interface is English only. The Italian translation and the interface-language setting in the General tab have been removed, along with the language machinery behind them: each page now ships one string table instead of two, and a missing string shows its key rather than rendering blank. Existing configurations keep working — the stored language value is simply ignored, so no settings are lost on upgrade. Italian season names are deliberately still recognised: "2ª Stagione", "2° Stagione" and "stagione 2" continue to resolve to season 2, because those are folder and series names read from your library rather than interface text, and dropping them would have silently broken season detection for Italian-named libraries. Release build with no warnings, 213 unit tests and 12 interface and accessibility tests; the browser count is down from 15 because the axe audit no longer runs every page twice, once per language. No breaking changes.

v1.1.0.0: New — openings and endings that animethemes.moe does not have can now be added by pasting a YouTube link into the Theme Finder: you are asked whether it is an OP or an ED, and whether you want audio, video or both. The feature is off by default and needs yt-dlp installed in the Jellyfin environment; the settings page reports whether it was found. Important data-loss fixes: an interrupted conversion no longer leaves a corrupt theme file that every later sync skipped as "already downloaded", with no sync or force sync able to repair it; deleting an item no longer wipes the theme-music and backdrops folders wholesale, which in a flat library destroyed every other item's themes and the user's own fanart; a force sync no longer deletes files it did not create, including those added through the Theme Finder; the cache and the unresolved list survive an abrupt shutdown. Themes whose download failed now stay in the Unresolved list instead of silently disappearing, and cancelling a sync leaves a finished state instead of a stuck progress bar. Also fixed: large theme videos are no longer cut off after 30 seconds, one provider erroring no longer stops resolution for the whole library, libraries with more than 100 items are no longer partly ignored, sequels and later seasons are no longer confidently bound to the wrong entry, and the playlist also finds items in subfolders. Interface: the ♪ button no longer polls the server every 1.5 seconds, keyboard use in the Theme Finder no longer selects the audio when triggering the preview or the video, and themes chosen across several seasons are attributed to the correct anime. No breaking changes.

v1.0.8.0: New unified high-contrast brand icon (comet plus musical note), shown consistently across every plugin page, the Theme Finder action and the Jellyfin dashboard sidebar. The icon is now a single embedded SVG asset instead of duplicated inline copies, and the sidebar entry no longer shows the generic folder. No breaking changes.

v1.0.7.1: Fixed secondary text contrast, with a stable WCAG AA margin that holds in CI renderers too. Stabilised the Playwright and axe audits by waiting for the asynchronous cache data and excluding in-flight animations. No breaking changes.

v1.0.7.0: Shared fail-closed frontend loader, reusable accessibility primitives, improved WCAG contrast and form fields, and corrected Theme Finder bulk actions. New Playwright suite with 13 end-to-end and axe tests. Full README with a language selector and official Buy Me a Coffee, PayPal and GitHub buttons. No breaking changes.

description:
Scans your library for gaps (missing movies in partially-owned collections and franchises, missing series content, unowned titles from actor and director filmographies, and related recommendations) using TMDB, Trakt, TheTVDB, and TVmaze, with music and book sources (MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, Discogs), and reads the watchlists and want-lists you already keep on those sites. versions.changelog: 10.11.10.0 - The Maintenance section has a Fulfillment queue for an administrator who fetches titles by hand. It folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, names who is still waiting, and shows the streaming-service icons as soon as the queue opens, with the same links a TODO row already has. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. name: Subtitle OCR
description:
Converts embedded image-based subtitle tracks (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to external SRT or ASS files using nOCR pattern matching. Pure managed code: no Tesseract and no native libraries, using the ffmpeg your server already ships. The .nocr database format is interchange-compatible with Subtitle Edit, so databases trained or corrected in its GUI drop straight in. A scheduled task scans your Movie and Episode libraries and writes a subtitle file beside each image-based track. OCR text is optionally spell-checked with Hunspell and corrected with Subtitle Edit's OCR fix lists, both fetched on demand.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 08:14 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IDisposable/jellyfin-plugin-subtitleocr/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/IDisposable/jellyfin-plugin-subtitleocr
overview: OCR image-based DVD and Blu-ray subtitles to SRT or ASS

versions.changelog:
Recognition is far more accurate and roughly three times faster. The bundled Latin database carries glyph shapes trained on real disc fonts, so few characters read as the unknown box. A file gives up every subtitle track in one pass rather than one pass per track, tracks recognize in parallel (Max parallelism leaves half the cores to playback), and image buffers are reused, so a run no longer drives the full garbage collections that interrupt playback. The matcher takes the best matching glyph rather than the first the database lists, reads case from the image's own x-height and cap height, splits a merged glyph pair, matches a multi-segment glyph on shape at any size, and follows the line's italic state so a stray mid-word italic reads as the run around it. Whether a track is light text on a dark outline or the reverse is read off the track itself, per track, so the Invert luma setting is gone, and word spacing is calibrated to real disc fonts.
Output keeps more of the disc. ASS carries the color the subtitles were drawn in as its style, with an override only on the lines that differ, places an off-center sign on the full alignment grid, escapes a literal brace, and rounds its timecodes; Auto picks ASS for a track that is positioned or uses more than one color. A cue never ends after the next one begins, a too-short cue is held to a 750 ms readable minimum, and a re-sent duplicate cue merges with its neighbor.
Text correction covers misread digits (a 1 between letters as l or I, a 0 as o), the two-letter words It, Is, In and If, a lowercase l after a speaker label, split contractions and quotes, punctuation spacing, a leading speaker dash, curly quotes, and padded sound-cue brackets. An accented Latin letter foreign to the track's language folds to its base ("Nothing" for "Nothińg"), keeping each language's own accents and leaving cast and character names alone. Spell-check protects names in singular and plural and runs before sentence casing, so a misread at the start of a line resolves against the dictionary instead of freezing into a name. The l-to-I fixes are English-only, so French keeps its elided articles. Language and hearing-impaired detection read a cue's words, not its markup, so close languages like Danish and Norwegian separate, and a track the database cannot really read is discarded rather than shipped.
The extraction log is its own dashboard page, with a Reprocess all button that runs the reprocess task and shows its progress, and a per-row reprocess for a single item. New settings: Fold foreign accents (on), and Aggressive OCR fixes (off) for the riskier digit twins 5/S and 8/B on a poorly scanned disc. The plugin is built against 10.11.0, the target ABI it declares, so it loads on every 10.11 server.

Output format is now selectable: SRT, ASS, or Auto, which decides per track and writes ASS only when a cue sits away from the bottom of the screen (PGS carries the position), so an ordinary track keeps the universally supported format. OCR text is spell-checked with Hunspell, protecting Title-case proper nouns and words drawn from the item's Jellyfin metadata (title, overview, series, cast and character names) so show and character names survive. Subtitle Edit OCR fix replace lists are applied when present; dictionaries and fix lists download on demand and re-download once older than a configurable age. A track with an undetermined language now has one detected from its OCR text and is named accordingly, and the track title, forced, hearing-impaired, and commentary flags appear in the file name so commentary tracks are identifiable. A hearing-impaired track is recognized from its own text when the source flags nothing, which is the norm for a remuxed disc. New OCR corrections cover misread apostrophes in contractions, mid-word capital X, V, and I, optional ellipsis folding, and bogus italic runs around single characters and punctuation. An unread glyph now costs nothing when matching a word against the dictionary, so "batt□e" resolves to "battle" and a damaged name can be restored from the item's metadata. A new "Reprocess extracted subtitles" task re-OCRs every logged file from its source with the current settings. Each file is probed with a single ffprobe pass rather than two, and only one OCR or reprocess task runs at a time.

Detect image-based subtitles by probing every Movie and Episode with ffprobe, since Jellyfin does not store PGS/VobSub streams in its metadata. A per-file cache skips files that are unchanged and were probed within a configurable window, with a force-rescan option. Word spacing now scales with subtitle line height, fixing spaces inserted between every letter on HD Blu-ray text. New options: extract only selected languages, discard a track whose dropped-event ratio is too high (removing any stale SRT), and a filename tag ({name}.{lang}.OCR.srt, shown as the subtitle title) so the plugin only ever overwrites or deletes its own output. A config-page modal lists every extracted file with a link to its movie or episode. The scheduled task now sits under its own category.

Initial production release. OCRs embedded image-based subtitles (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to SRT files using nOCR pattern matching, with Subtitle Edit-compatible .nocr databases. Pure managed code: no Tesseract, no native dependencies. Optionally skips image tracks whose language already has a text subtitle.

versions.changelog:
### Added

- A Quality column that names the class a frame falls in, from 144p to 8K, with an i in place of the p for interlaced video. It sorts by class rather than by how the name reads, and a filter picks a class from a list and holds rows at, above or below it. (#7)
- `Schema` answers the classes a quality can be held against, in their order.
- A failed export and a failed column save are reported in words of their own.

### Changed

- A CSV names the unit of a size, a runtime and a bitrate in its header. An ODS shows a runtime as a time, counted in hours past a day, and a size and a bitrate with their unit, all of them still numbers a spreadsheet can total. (#6)
- A number typed into a filter with the digit grouping the table prints is read as one number, so 48,000 is no longer 48.
- The README describes `search` and what an export holds, and names bytes per hour and truth values among the filter values.
- An advisory against a package Jellyfin brings along is a build warning rather than an error.

### Fixed

- The sidebar entry followed a language further down the browser's list when English came first, and could take one the browser had ruled out.
- A book ran for the second Jellyfin measures its reading progress in, and was given a size per hour from it.
- A series whose episodes run at 24000/1001 and at 2997/125 read as mixed in its frame rate, though every episode shows 23.976.
- A DVD or Blu-ray folder weighed only the first file of its title. It now weighs every file in the folder and shows no size per hour.
- A .strm took its bitrate and its size per hour from the bytes of the text file.
- The table kept its scroll position when a page turn, a sort, a search or a filter replaced its rows.
- A visit whose schema failed to load left an empty page behind, and a later one left the filter button disabled.
- Two quick changes to the rows per page or to the level a tab is expanded to could be stored in the wrong order.
- The spacing of the tab counts, the column picker and the row toggles did not follow a right-to-left layout.
- Three checks could not fail or skipped part of what they name: the rounded runtime of a series, the version in the README badge, and the names of the tabs.
- A failed library refresh ended the test run, a request the server never answered held it for good, and Ctrl-C waited for the helper container to finish.
- The fixture recipe of the screenshot script went on after a failed encode, and the version list did not retry a connection that dropped after the request was sent.

### Dependencies

- jsdom 30.1.1 in the tests. (#4)
- Renovate keeps `test/` in its scan through an empty `ignorePaths` rather than `ignorePresets`.

### Added

- Conditions on any column, up to twenty per request: at least, at most, equals, differs from, contains, does not contain, is empty and is not empty, whichever of them fit the column. A value is typed in the unit the table shows, a filtered tab lists the level it is expanded to, flat, and an export writes exactly those rows.
- Inventory has its own entry in the dashboard sidebar, worded in the language the browser asks in.
- The table opens on the Inventory logo, worded in the language the page is in and linking to the project.
- Music filed loose beside the albums is listed with them, since no row opens to reach it.
- The plugin archive carries its image, so the catalog and the plugins page show the logo rather than an empty tile.
- `Schema` answers the conditions each column can be held against and how many of them one request may carry.

### Changed

- The Music tab counts tracks rather than albums, and is called Music rather than Albums.
- The table fills the window, with its header held in place while the rows scroll.
- Plays and Plays (all users) read 0 rather than an empty cell, so a condition and a sort can hold them.
- Size, duration and bitrate are held against a range rather than an exact value, which a column shown rounded to a unit could never meet.
- A number is typed with a decimal comma where the language uses one, and a value that cannot be read is marked rather than quietly dropped.
- Leaving the page and coming back finds the tab the way it was left, with its sort and its page.
- Every text cell of a CSV is quoted once it holds a separator, whichever one the file itself uses.
- A film or episode kept in several cuts, any of them split into parts, reports the bytes of every file. It and the folders above it show no size per hour, and its bitrate is that of the cut being served.
- A manual install is described by the plugins folder of the server's data directory, rather than by the Docker path alone.
- Bug reports ask for the steps, a screenshot and the log lines; a pull request agrees to the contributor license agreement by checkbox, which a workflow checks.

### Fixed

- A filtered table of fewer than five rows collapsed to nothing on a low window.
- A film grouped with a version in another library was weighed twice on Jellyfin 12.1.
- A film played in its second cut showed no play count and no date, though Jellyfin counts it played.
- Firefox showed rows above the table header after a wheel scroll.
- A second address for the page bound its controls to the view the web client had kept, leaving the new one empty.
- A page turned inside the pause after typing a condition left the table behind the end of what it lists.
- A page left behind by a library that shrank falls back to the last page there is.
- A condition on a column a plugin update no longer offers took the whole page down, on that visit and every later one.
- The page stops offering conditions once the server would refuse another.
- Exports in Arabic and Persian wrote a decimal separator no spreadsheet reads.
- A download the browser gave up on is no longer logged as a server error.
- A failed request no longer leaves another tab's rows on screen or skips the page, sort and total that are drawn, and the column picker no longer stores a selection for a level that is not shown.
- An expanded row closes again when the table it was opened in is replaced, and expansion requests left over from another tab are no longer sent.
- A numeric first column is no longer right-aligned where rows expand, which hid their indentation, and height is printed without digit grouping.
- The API rejects `parentIds` as soon as one id is not a guid.
- The first build of a table asks which library a folder belongs to once rather than once per item in it.

### Security

- A name holding a semicolon or a tab could start a formula in a spreadsheet set to split there, since only the separator of the file itself was quoted.
- An invented culture name on an export answered with an error and grew a cache that is never freed, and a lone surrogate in a condition answered with an error as well. Both are refused now.
- A configuration saved through Jellyfin's own endpoint with empty lists made every endpoint of the plugin fail until the next restart.

### Dependencies

- Renovate follows the Node, jsdom and Playwright versions the tests are pinned to, alongside the GitHub Actions and the analyzers it already tracked.

### Added

- Rows per page, chosen in the footer and kept across restarts, from 50 up to 10000.
- Three columns totalling playback over every account on the server: how often something was played, when it last was, and how many accounts have played it to the end, which on a folder counts only the accounts that have played everything below it.
- The tab whose rows are on their way and the export being built now show that they are working.
- `Schema` reports the culture it answered in, which is what the page takes its plural form from.

### Changed

- What was labelled Played is now Fully played, since Jellyfin only ticks it when something ran to the end.
- The export is written to a temporary file rather than built in memory, and stops when the browser goes away.
- `Items` and `Export` refuse a sort column they do not know instead of quietly sorting by the first one.
- Every change is tested against each Jellyfin release from 12.0 on, one run per major and minor version, taken from the published image tags.

### Fixed

- A film split across several files reported the size of the first file alone, and no runtime at all.
- A trailer or a making of sitting beside a film was listed as an item of its own, in a tab of its own, and its bytes counted towards the totals.
- The frame rate could read 1000 fps where Jellyfin's own interface shows the real one.
- An item Jellyfin marks played on reaching the end of playback did not reach the table until the next stop report.
- The two dropdowns had no arrow, the search field put an empty label into the toolbar, and a disabled button looked exactly like one that could be clicked.
- A first load that failed left the page blank, with an empty column picker behind the Columns button.
- Expanding a level asked for every fifty rows at once, so a large page could open hundreds of requests at a time.
- A row that turned out to have nothing below it lost its control, its alignment with the rows around it, and the keyboard focus.
- A long path was never shortened, and the footer could not wrap in a narrow window.
- The page indicator is announced when it changes, and the control that opens a row says which row it opens.

### Dependencies

- The release archive is uploaded with the gh CLI; softprops/action-gh-release is no longer used.

### Added

- One table in the dashboard listing everything in the libraries, from a whole series down to a single episode, with 38 columns across General, Video, Audio, Subtitles and Playback.
- Folder rows total what is below them: size, runtime and item count add up, an attribute the children disagree on reads as Mixed, and playback folds from the episodes or tracks underneath.
- A column selection per level and how far a tab opens, both remembered across restarts.
- Search across every level of a tab, sorting on any column, and paging.
- Export of the current view as CSV or ODS, in the language of the interface.
- English, German, Spanish, French and Italian.

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

versions.changelog:
v3.0.0.4 - Per-library file counts, boxset link fix

- The Per-Library Breakdown now shows a file count below every size value (trickplay folders included), so sparse and dense libraries are distinguishable at a glance
- Boxset library rows no longer link into the Library Explorer, whose scope excludes boxsets; they render as plain text instead of opening an empty state
- Every task dropdown in Settings now explains what the task does, via an info button next to each task name, in all dashboard languages
- The Overview Trickplay card now also shows the space used by trickplay images Jellyfin stores internally, on its own line below the alongside-media total, marked with an (internal) badge, or as the headline when no alongside data exists
- Compact log view on phones: log entries stack as cards below 700 px instead of squeezing into a four-column table, so no horizontal scrolling is needed, and rows keep breathing room at the screen edges
- Roomier Library Explorer filter popovers on phones using nearly the full viewport width, like the bitrate editor
- Tested by 6219 unit tests and 352 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.3 - Library Explorer, new Codecs breakdowns, disabled users ignored

- The Codecs tab now has a Library Explorer: combine resolution, codecs, bitrate, languages, watched users and formats into one search, scoped to the libraries you pick in its multi-select, so you can find e.g. all 4K films with low bitrate
- Options with zero matches under the other filters are hidden automatically, dimensions without matches stay greyed out, and multi-value dropdowns accept several audio languages, subtitle languages or users at once
- Every active filter is shown in the result header and a Reset button clears the whole search; results arrive as the familiar grouped file tree with Movies, TV Shows and other sections
- Jump straight into the search from the Overview: each library name and all four media cards open the Explorer pre-filtered to that scope
- Every categorical filter can be negated with Includes/Excludes, so you can search e.g. audio languages that are not German; excluded picks show as ≠ pills and counts preview what stays
- Four new breakdowns in the Codecs tab, each with drill-down to the exact files: Video Bitrate (7 tiers from < 2 to > 60 Mbps), Audio Languages, Subtitle Languages and Watched (by username plus Never watched)
- Each bitrate tier uses what Jellyfin measured for the video stream; when a file has no per-stream value the average is estimated from its size and runtime, so almost every file lands in a real tier instead of Unknown
- Disabled Jellyfin users no longer skew results: their old plays are excluded from Smart Recommendations, watch history and the new Watched breakdown
- Long breakdowns start collapsed behind a Show-all toggle with Unknown always last, and unreadable language tags fold into Unknown instead of junk entries
- Added responsive, independently scrollable library result cards.
- Improved compact layouts for mobile controls.
- Added consistent themed scrollbar styling across plugin panels and lists.
- The Overview Per-Library Breakdown has a new Other column per library covering NFO files, text files and other unrecognized sidecar files, plus a Books column whenever a book library exists, so every row adds up exactly to its Total
- Tested by 6169 unit tests and 341 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.2 - Log tab, save bar, resolution and touch fixes

- Clearing the plugin log no longer briefly shows a false "Failed to clear logs." error: the Clear button now confirms success immediately and refreshes the view right away
- Genuine clear failures (e.g. expired session or server error) now write a structured diagnostic to the browser console with the HTTP status and error kind, alongside the visible red button feedback, so a real problem is never silent
- Save bar no longer crowds on phones: the unsaved-changes label and Save button now stack on narrow screens, so long translations like the German "Nicht gespeichert" are no longer cut off
- Widescreen films are counted at their real resolution: cinemascope masters like 1920x800 or 1920x1040 are now correctly shown as 1080p instead of 720p in the Codecs tab, decided by whichever axis reaches a resolution class
- The resolution drill-down now lists each file's exact pixel dimensions (e.g. 1920x800) next to its name, readable on desktop and phones
- Chart tooltips work reliably on touch: the first tap on the Trends chart or a Codecs ring now shows and keeps the tooltip instead of flashing it away, and a second tap on the same Codecs segment closes it
- The save confirmation only appears after a real save: reverting a setting back to its original value no longer briefly shows "All changes saved"
- Tested by 5535 unit tests and 320 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.1 - Per-instance library allocation for Arr

- Assign specific Jellyfin libraries to each Radarr/Sonarr instance, so the Arr tab compares an instance only against the libraries it manages
- With two or more instances of a type, each gets a picker in Settings listing only the matching kind of library (movies for Radarr, TV for Sonarr)
- Leave a picker empty to keep it automatic: instances are matched to libraries from their root folders
- Assignments are kept across backup and restore
- Fixes a 4K instance flagging every 1080p film as "not in Radarr"
- Tested by 5499 unit tests and 318 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.0 - Major release for Jellyfin 12.0+

- Books in your library overview: eBook libraries now show their size and file count on the Overview tab and count towards your storage totals, and they're always protected from every cleanup task
- Smarter recommendations: a much bigger model, fairer suggestions for brand-new users, and more variety in your top picks (no more ten near-identical films in a row)
- Recommendations now also learn from franchises/collections, country of origin, collection & folder themes, whether a series is finished or ongoing, writers/creators, top-billed cast, and how rare a genre or studio is in your library (each signal is optional per item, so missing metadata never skews a pick)
- Fresh picks appear between nightly runs, and faster generation on big libraries
- Redesigned Settings, Health and Arr tabs with a live 'reachable' indicator, plus a sticky save bar and unsaved-changes warning
- Better on phones
- Stronger security: API keys are never shown to the browser, backups can leave keys out, and cleanup can never delete or touch anything outside your media libraries
- Safer trash and cleanup: turning retention off really turns it off, trashing a shortcut never removes the file it points to, and Windows shortcut handling is fixed
- More accurate library stats and safer Seerr request cleanup
- More reliable saves and backups (no more rare 'lost save' when antivirus is scanning)
- New end-to-end test suite runs the plugin inside a real Jellyfin 12 server on every change and proves cleanup stays inside your libraries
- Note: your recommendation model retrains from scratch after upgrading, so suggestions settle back in over the next scheduled runs
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v2.1.0.6: Diagnostics for reverse-proxy / WAF-blocked config saves. Added GET /JellyfinHelper/Ping liveness endpoint. Configuration model-binding and validation errors are now logged to the plugin log (source "API", level WARN) instead of silently returning 400. Frontend save handler now classifies errors (network / proxy / server / unauthorized) and surfaces the HTTP status and body snippet to the console, with an automatic Ping follow-up to distinguish "backend unreachable" from "backend reachable, payload rejected". 2325 tests.

v2.1.0.5: Fix StackOverflow on circular symlinks in directory scan. Fix IOException on long trash path names. Added Swedish (sv) language. Exclude Libraries multi-select dropdown. Trash folder browser. Trash path change dialog (move/delete content on path change). Enhanced trash path validation. Upgraded to Jellyfin 10.11.10. 2318 tests.
v2.1.0.4: Fix MissingMethodException for IUserManager.Users.

v2.1.0.3: Add TMDB and Seerr deep links on discovery card flip-back (opens system browser on mobile). Fix 400 Bad Request when submitting discovery requests on Seerr instances with 0-based server IDs. Fix duplicate quality profiles in selection popup for users with multiple root folders. Add graceful error handling for Jellyfin version incompatibility in watch history collection. 2206 tests
v2.1.0.2: Improved Discovery Sidebar Navigation - tab layout can show more than 5 recommendations in one row now. Automatically reloading next recommendation after one was dismissed or requested.
v2.1.0.1: Fix Discovery sidebar navigation - tab is now found dynamically by container index regardless of user-configured tab name, instead of relying on exact text match.

v2.1.0.0: Seerr Discovery - personalized external content recommendations via Overseerr/Jellyseerr with ensemble scoring, one-click request submission, parental rating enforcement, language-based discovery, and Arr library exclusion. 2190 tests.

v2.0.0.3: Instance-based Arr config (legacy removed), persistent language/log-level. Recommendations add audio language & creation date, subtitle language affinity, collection progression boost; meaningful-interaction watched predicates. Centralized popularity scoring, richer training features (31-feature vector), series aggregation, weight schema bump. Neural MLP upgraded to 4-hidden-layer architecture (31→48→24→12→6→1, ~3097 params). Training refactored into TrainingDataBuilder + TrainingFeatureComputer. A/B testing cohort infrastructure with deterministic user bucketing and adaptive sigmoid midpoint. 2124 tests.

v2.0.0.2: Replaced decorative emojis with Material Symbols font icons for consistent cross-platform rendering. Standardized dash punctuation. Fixed subtitle orphan detection to avoid false deletions. 2110 tests.
v2.0.0.1: UI improvement - Recommendations and Watch Activity sections in the Discover tab are now collapsible. Collapsible state is preserved on user switch. 2032 tests.

v2.0.0.0: New Discover tab using an ensemble ML model to provide tailored content recommendations. This update also introduces granular activity tracking and improved system cleanup for uninstallation of this plugin. 2032 tests.

v1.2.1.0: Statistics refactored to use Jellyfin MediaStream metadata (replaces filename parsing). Dynamic range detection (HDR10, HDR10+, Dolby Vision, HLG, SDR). Extended resolution classification (8K, 1440p, SD). Differentiated audio codecs (TrueHD Atmos, DTS-X, DTS-HD MA, EAC3 Atmos). Donut chart enhancements with dynamic range visualization. Library Insights in Trends tab (top-10 largest directories, recently added/changed items, per-library size breakdown with 15-min cache). Performance improvement via per-item video stream caching. Documentation updated.

v1.2.0.0: Seerr Cleanup Task (scheduled cleanup of unavailable Overseerr/Jellyseerr media requests), Unsaved Settings Alert (dirty-tracking with discard/save/cancel dialog), Collapsible Arr/Seerr sections with dynamic instance count, Auto-Save Dropdowns (task modes + language save instantly with checkmark/cross indicator), Link Repair enhanced with symlink support, Auto-Init Scan on first visit, Scroll Position Restore after language change and backup import, 4-part versioning, meta.json fixes.
v1.1.0: Performance optimizations for GrowthTimelineService and BackupService, refactored monolith services, improved cross-platform compatibility, Trends UI enhancements.

v1.0.9: Removed legacy statistics history (replaced by growth timeline), removed Export/CSV endpoints, new StatisticsCacheService, legacy history file cleanup, growth timeline interpolation & deduplication, reduced backup size limit, 957 tests.
v1.0.8: Project restructure, bug fix for Jellyfin versions below 10.11.8, backup/restore data, enhanced TrendChart, relocated download buttons, responsive Data Tree for touch devices.

v1.0.7: Added i18n support (EN, DE, FR, ES, PT, TR, ZH), scheduled task for cleaning empty media folders, trend chart visualization, configurable intervals, and automatic plugin data directory creation.
Exclude trash folders from media statistics, fix false positives for orphaned TV show metadata directories, fix trash disable dialog in UI.

Multi-instance Arr support (up to 3 Radarr + 3 Sonarr), Arr connection test endpoint, persisted latest scan results (survives restarts), post-cleanup statistics scan, embedded subtitle detection in health checks, video vs music audio codec split, codec file path tracking with clickable drill-down, trash contents detail API, trash folder management UI, trash disable dialog, other file tracking, 6-tab modular dashboard (Overview/Codecs/Health/Trends/Settings/Arr), modular CSS/JS build system, XSS protection, boxset/collection health check skipping, comprehensive README rewrite, 573 tests.

Added STRM file repair task, unified TaskMode system (Activate/DryRun/Deactivate per task), single master HelperCleanupTask replacing separate scheduled tasks, fixed ConfigVersion not preserved on settings save, fixed DI resolution for System.IO.Abstractions.IFileSystem, updated README, 315 tests.

Fixed plugin logo 404 (logo.png now included as physical file in release ZIP with meta.json imagePath), fixed SanitizeFileName null-char handling, removed duplicate Cleanup Statistics UI section, removed unused GetThumbImage method, 244 tests.

Fixed subtitle false positives (explicit ISO 639 allowlists instead of naive 2-3 letter heuristic), moved SubtitleFlags/KnownLanguageCodes to MediaExtensions, ArrIntegrationService now uses IHttpClientFactory, CleanupTrackingService thread-safety with lock, specific exception handling, removed _ = ex anti-pattern, 244 tests.
Fixed config page not loading (script/style tags moved inside page div), plugin now visible in Jellyfin sidebar menu with EnableInMainMenu, updated test count to 212.

Initial release with trickplay folder cleanup, empty media folder cleanup, orphaned subtitle cleaner, media statistics dashboard, audio codec analysis, export (JSON/CSV), historical trends, trash/recycle bin, Arr stack integration (Radarr/Sonarr), multi-language dashboard (en/de/fr/es/pt/zh/tr), library include/exclude lists, and 196 tests.
