versions.changelog:
## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Features
- Generated posters now appear in the episodes Edit Images dialog, so you can pick the frame you want instead of refreshing until you get a good one
- Choose how many alternate posters to offer in Edit Images, from 1 to 10 (default 3)
- Brush style can outline its stroke, sharing the Cutout styles outline toggle
- Element Spacing setting controls the gap between stacked poster elements, so every style spaces them the same way
- The font dropdown now lists the fonts actually installed on your server, and a font that is not installed is called out in the log instead of silently rendering in a substitute face
- Overlay colors collapse to an opacity control when Palette-Derived Colors is on, since the color itself comes from the image

## Breaking
- The scheduled task has been removed. Poster generation now runs entirely as a metadata provider - use a library metadata refresh, or pick a poster from Edit Images
- Processing history and its database have been removed, along with the Reset Processing History button. Jellyfins own refresh options now decide what gets regenerated

## Fixes
- Deleting an episode poster no longer left it permanently blank; there is no tracking state left to say the episode was already done
- Changing a custom font now takes effect; it used to be left out of the change detection entirely
- A tall logo no longer overlaps the episode code beneath it
- Long episode titles wrap to two lines again instead of being shortened to one
- Short titles no longer leave a gap between the episode code and the title
- Cancelling a refresh now stops frame extraction instead of letting it run to completion
- Generated posters are no longer written to the transcode directory and left behind
- Aspect ratios like 2.35:1 now parse correctly on servers with a comma decimal separator
- Saving the Posters tab no longer hangs on a spinner when the save fails, and no longer overwrites the settings on the other tab
- Settings added in a newer version no longer break saving for configurations written by an older one

## Developer
- The frosted panel shape and the brush stroke paths are disposed even when an exception unwinds
- Poster elements are positioned by a shared measure-then-place layout column instead of each style walking its own offsets, and titles are fitted to the height they are given as well as the width
- Poster configuration is never written back during plugin startup, so a failed config load can no longer overwrite good settings with defaults
- Poster rendering returns encoded bytes rather than temp files
- Removed the scheduled task, tracking database, configuration hashing, and around 900 lines of superseded code
- Shaders, mask filters, and image filters are disposed rather than left to finalization; HDR brightening no longer round-trips the whole bitmap through managed memory
- Example templates carry every current setting, and the bundled examples were regenerated
- Test suite grown from 21 to 39 cases, covering layout, title fitting, aspect ratio parsing, font resolution, and the generated image cache
- Bump Base to 2026.7.31

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12

## Fixes
- Remove backdrops before using the current extracted frame as the new backdrop to prevent image bloat

## Fixes
- Frame seeking starts from a random phase each run, so refreshing an episode image picks a new frame instead of the same one

## Features
- Abbreviate tries the text before a divider, then the first sentence, then initials with periods

## Fixes
- Episode numbers and codes are pinned so title length cannot move them in any style
- Fade titles wrap to two vertical rows before long title handling engages

## Features

## Polish

- New poster style - Frosted Glass - blurred glass panel behind the episode text

- New poster style - Timeline - progress bar showing the episodes position within the season

- Tracking database uses WAL mode, pooled connections, and a batched filter pass

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0

Fix 3.2 build issues.

## Developer
- Server routes moved under the Allow system access toggle, so a page needs one permission instead of two
- Shortened the configuration page help text

## Features
- Allow local resource calls, so a page can define named server side routes and call them with serverFetch while the server forwards each to its configured target
- Optional per page Allow system access toggle that runs a page without the sandbox, so its scripts can call the Jellyfin API and reach other resources on this origin
- Pages on a signed in tier can now be restricted to named users, defaulting to all users at that tier

## Developer
- Defining a route also runs its page unsandboxed, since the helper cannot reach the route from an opaque origin
- A route credential stored before encryption existed is upgraded on the next save rather than left in the clear
- Route credentials are encrypted at rest and never sent to a browser, and the configuration page posts back a sentinel so an untouched field keeps the stored value
- Forwarded requests carry the caller's headers minus a deny list, so the viewer's Jellyfin session is never handed to a route target
- Route targets must be absolute http or https URLs fixed in configuration, so a page cannot turn a route into an open proxy
- A restricted page is refused before its body is rendered, so content never reaches a viewer the list does not name
- An allow list is refused on an anonymous page at save time, and fails closed at serve time if the stored list is unusable
- Pages stay sandboxed by default, and an unsandboxed page still reaches the browser HTML encoded inside the wrapper's srcdoc
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Developer
- Serve every page under one Content-Security-Policy so a page behaves the same at any visibility tier
- Allow pages to load external resources and submit forms, which the anonymous tier previously blocked
- Allow pages to be embedded by the Jellyfin origin (frame-ancestors 'self')
- Serve page HTML as UTF-8 so single-file documents without a charset meta tag render correctly
- Sign in correctly when the web client is signed in to more than one server
- Reject unknown visibility tiers and malformed asset content types when configuration is saved
- Key the decoded asset cache to the asset itself, closing a stale-bytes window around a save

## Developer

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Fixed
- The plain-http warning no longer logs the request URL's authority, which carried the update secret into the server log for providers whose credential lives in the URL's userinfo (ClouDNS DynURL, Directnic gateway URL). The warning now names the record's hostname instead
- A Data Protection key store that fails for an unexpected reason surfaces instead of being silently downgraded to plaintext credential storage; the expected failures (bad path, no permission, no service) still fall back as before

## Developer
- Address the outstanding CodeQL findings across the plugin and test projects (LINQ filtering and projection, ternary assignment, dictionary lookup, response disposal in the HTTP test stub)

## Fixed
- Resolve the TTL "1 = automatic" sentinel to a per-provider default instead of sending a literal one-second TTL (Gandi, GoDaddy, Spaceship, Hetzner, DNSExit)
- Yandex matches records by type as well as name, so an IPv4 update can no longer overwrite an AAAA or TXT record, and A/AAAA now update independently
- Spaceship writes the new record before removing stale ones, so a failed update leaves the old address serving instead of deleting the record
- Hetzner treats an accepted, still-applying action as success instead of timing out and counting a false failure toward backoff
- DNS Made Easy treats "no update required" as success instead of walking a healthy record into backoff
- DDNS.fm validates the response body instead of treating any HTTP 200 as success
- NS1 record creation sends the required zone, domain, and type fields, so first-time setup works
- Apex hostnames infer the correct domain when no zone is set (Porkbun, Dynadot, Spaceship, Dinahosting), and Dinahosting gained an optional Zone field
- OVH DynHost, DynDNS v1, DSLReports, and NearlyFreeSpeech.NET declare IPv4-only, so an IPv6 address is no longer recorded as pushed and endlessly re-pushed
- A record with one working address family is no longer paused by backoff when only the other family fails

## Developer
- Harden the publish workflow (release body via env, tag-derived version, fail-fast asset downloads, required tag on manual dispatch)
- Slash-command dispatch uses the JF_BOT_TOKEN secret instead of a placeholder
- CI packages with build.sh and verifies the zip contents, and build.sh parses build.yaml colon- and space-safely

Features:
- New rule field: Aspect Ratio (under Video). Filter by a video's display
  aspect ratio such as 16:9 or 2.35:1. Comparisons are proportional, so
  "less than 1:1" matches every portrait video and "greater than 1:1" every
  landscape one - no need to list each ratio.
- Live TV Channel media type for smart collections. Group channels from any
  Live TV tuner into a collection with rules such as Name, Tags or Is
  Favorite. Collections only - Jellyfin playlists cannot hold channels
  (#290).
- "Hide when empty" is now "Min Items": a list stays hidden until it holds
  at least that many items, instead of only while it is completely empty.
  Found under Limits next to Max Items, with a matching default in
  Settings. Existing lists keep their current behaviour with no changes
  needed.

Bug Fixes:
- MDBList official list URLs (mdblist.com/lists/official/movies/... and
  .../shows/...) returned no items. They now load, and the JustWatch
  Streaming Charts list keeps the country, period, provider and genre
  filters from the pasted URL (#525).

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

Same plugin as v12.0.1.0 - no functional changes. It exists so that servers
upgraded from Jellyfin 10.11 to Jellyfin 12 automatically pick up the correct
build.

Bug Fixes:
- Upgrading Jellyfin from 10.11 to 12 left the plugin showing "Not supported".
  Each release published its 10.11 and its 12 build under the same version
  number, so a server that had installed the 10.11 build kept it after the
  upgrade - Jellyfin saw no newer version to offer, and the 10.11 build cannot
  run on Jellyfin 12. This release is published for Jellyfin 12 only, so those
  servers now see an update and repair themselves. Jellyfin 10.11 servers are
  unaffected and stay on v12.0.1.0.

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

The first stable release for Jellyfin 12, and the biggest update yet - 22 release
candidates of work since v10.11.30.2. Jellyfin 10.11 is still fully supported.

Jellyfin 12:
- Full support for Jellyfin 12, including the final 12.0.0 release
- Jellyfin 10.11 continues to receive the same updates

New features:
- List templates: one-click starting points on the Create tab
- Hide when empty: a list disappears while nothing matches, and returns on its own
- Group results into collections: turn an item search into a collection of collections
- Collection and Playlist media types: build collections of collections or playlists
- Smart collections now carry genres, studios, parental rating and total runtime
- Smart list badge on generated covers, with a setting to turn it off
- Integration API so other tools can create and manage smart lists
- Bumpers, and random group selection
- New rule field: User Rating
- Date rules can include items whose date is missing from metadata
- New settings for default media types and for hiding new lists when empty

External lists:
- New providers: ListenBrainz and Scrob
- Music lists match tracks via MusicBrainz, one library item per matched track
- User-Agent setting for when a provider starts blocking requests

Sorting:
- Least Recently Watched Round Robin, and Shuffled Round Robin
- Round Robin can group by Collection and order items within each group
- Crossover episodes that aired close together play back-to-back, with an Air Window setting
- Play Count (all users) and Last Played (all users)

Improvements:
- Large speed-up for expensive rules - people, languages, resolution and more are read once per refresh
- Parent tags, studios and genres are found at every level above an item, including the library
- Only fully watched episodes advance the Least Recently Watched rotation
- Weekly cleanup removes leftover playlists and collections whose list is gone
- Rule groups are named consistently throughout; the sort option is now Rule Group Order

Bug fixes:
- Titles containing numbers sort correctly - "Season 2" before "Season 10"
- The Resolution sort did nothing and left lists sorted by name
- Episodes came back unordered when Season/Episode was combined with another sort
- A series showed a play count of 0 even when every episode was watched
- Items with no release date no longer match "before", "older than" and "not equals"
- IMDb lists, charts and awards failed to load with a "Forbidden" error
- Configuration pages loaded blank behind a reverse proxy, or with Cloudflare Rocket Loader
- Smart collections disappeared when the TMDbBoxSets plugin was installed
- Duplicates left behind by a failed deletion are detected and cleaned up
- List names can contain : * ? < > | " / and \ again
- Saving a list now reports why it failed instead of appearing to do nothing
- A failed save no longer discards what you typed
- Deleting a list right after editing it no longer brings it back

Existing lists may change:
- Rules checking parent values now look at every level above an item, so they match more
- Music lists are the most visible case: artist folder and library values now count
- Similar To applies within its own rule group instead of filtering the whole list
- Smart collections now carry aggregated genres/studios/runtime, so other lists may match them
- Include-only checkboxes are migrated automatically to Name rules

name: Shoko
description:
A Jellyfin plugin to integrate [Jellyfin](https://jellyfin.org/docs/) with [Shoko Server](https://shokoanime.com/downloads/shoko-server/).
## Read this before installing
**This plugin requires that you have already set up and are using Shoko Server**, and that the files you intend to include in Jellyfin are **indexed** (and optionally managed) by Shoko Server. **Otherwise, the plugin won't be able to provide metadata for your files**, since there is no metadata to find for them.

versions.changelog: Add support for 12.1

# 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

# 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.
* Jellyfin 12 support includes both the **classic Desktop layout** and the newer **modern React/MUI layout**.
* A compatible **File Transformation 3.x** release is required.
* If you're using the **Get updates early** option, unreleased upstream Media Bar changes may behave differently from the frontend bundled and tested with this plugin release.

## Contributors

* austinnorgaard
* judarange

## ❤️ Support

If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27).

Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed injected menu items not closing the Jellyfin user-menu popover after navigation (PR #20, @n00bcodr).
* Fixed Plugin Pages injection sometimes failing on clients where jQuery had not finished loading, including affected Android clients (PR #20, @n00bcodr).
* Added cache-busting to the injected script so clients reliably receive updated versions.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* Dropped support for Jellyfin 10.11 releases prior to 10.11.11. Jellyfin 10.11.11 remains supported.

### Contributors

* n00bcodr

# 🧭 Plugin Pages, Ready for Jellyfin 12 Plugin Pages **3.0.0.0** brings the plugin forward for **Jellyfin 12**, updating the way custom pages are injected into the Jellyfin web client and fixing the user-facing plugin settings flow for Jellyfin's latest architecture. This release also drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7**, while introducing a new plugin-facing API that makes it much easier for other plugins to add and manage their own pages. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**. * Added a new public **Plugin Interface** allowing other plugins to register pages programmatically through `PluginInterface.RegisterPage(JObject)`. * Added `PluginInterface.RemovePage(string id)`, allowing plugins to unregister pages they previously registered. * Updated Plugin Pages' web-client injection to work with the changes introduced in Jellyfin 12. * Updated user-facing plugin settings pages to work with Jellyfin 12. * Updated the underlying Jellyfin dependencies and integration points required by the new server/web-client architecture. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Reworked page injection to account for changes to the Jellyfin 12 web client. * Improved compatibility for plugins that use Plugin Pages to expose user-facing pages inside Jellyfin. * Updated the user plugin settings integration so pages opened through Jellyfin's user menu continue to behave correctly on Jellyfin 12. * Dependent plugins can now manage their pages at runtime rather than directly modifying Plugin Pages' configuration. * Cleaned up legacy compatibility code that is no longer required now that older Jellyfin versions are being dropped. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed custom plugin pages failing to inject correctly into the **Jellyfin 12** web client. * Fixed user-facing plugin settings pages not working correctly on Jellyfin 12. * Fixed cases where pages registered through Plugin Pages could result in a **Page not found** experience after Jellyfin web-client changes. * Fixed compatibility issues caused by changes to Jellyfin's client-side routing and page-loading behaviour. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility Plugin Pages now provides a public plugin-facing API for registering and removing pages. * `PluginInterface.RegisterPage(JObject)` can be used to register a page directly with Plugin Pages. * The supplied `JObject` is deserialised into Plugin Pages' `PluginPage` model and registered immediately with the page manager. * `PluginInterface.RemovePage(string id)` can be used to unregister an existing page by its ID. * Plugins no longer need to directly modify `Jellyfin.Plugin.PluginPages/config.json` in order to dynamically add their own pages. * Plugins can now register pages during startup and remove them again during shutdown or when their configuration changes. This should be considered the **preferred integration path for dependent plugins going forward**, replacing direct manipulation of Plugin Pages' configuration where possible. The new API is additive, so existing configuration-based integrations are not inherently broken by the update. Plugin developers are, however, encouraged to migrate to the new interface for cleaner lifecycle management and better compatibility with future Plugin Pages releases. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**. * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier Plugin Pages release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Plugin Pages continues to require a compatible version of **File Transformation**. * Plugins that depend on Plugin Pages should also be updated to versions compatible with Jellyfin 12. * The new `PluginInterface` is additive; plugins using the previous configuration-based approach can continue to work, but the programmatic API is now the recommended integration method. ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

# 🔥 The Biggest Home Screen Sections Update Yet This is the biggest Home Screen Sections update to date, bringing a substantial set of new features, fixes, localisation improvements, and internal changes alongside support for Jellyfin 12. With this release, Home Screen Sections is moving to **3.0.0.0**, marking a major step forward for the plugin and laying the groundwork for future Jellyfin versions. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**, including updated dependencies and compatibility changes required by the new Jellyfin version. * Added a new **Collections** section to display collections from the user's library. * Added a new **Recently Added In Library** section, allowing recently added media to be displayed for individual libraries, including custom libraries such as Anime (#231). * Added routing to supported sections, allowing section headers such as Genre to link through to their relevant Jellyfin pages. * Added per-section settings, allowing individual sections to have their own configurable behaviour. * Improved **Because You Watched** recommendations with a scoring system to better prioritise similar titles. * Added an option for **Recently Added Shows** to display either shows or individual episodes (#38). * Added an option to filter Upcoming sections based on the user's Jellyfin library access (#214, PR #249, @n00bcodr). * Added warnings when required plugin dependencies cannot be found (#234). * Added separate admin display names for sections, allowing their names to be translated without affecting the title displayed on the home screen. * Integrated with the new **Plugin Pages PluginInterface**, allowing Home Screen Sections to manage its Plugin Pages integration programmatically. ## 🛠️ Improvements * The **Modular Home** menu entry is now registered dynamically through Plugin Pages rather than relying on static Plugin Pages configuration. * The Modular Home page can now be added and removed as part of Home Screen Sections' own lifecycle, reducing the chance of stale or missing Plugin Pages entries. * Improved the reliability of the **Modular Home** link and its integration with Jellyfin's user-facing plugin settings flow. Previous releases have seen cases where the link was missing or resulted in a `Page not found` page. * Home Screen Sections now respects libraries a user has chosen to hide from their home screen, filtering them from relevant sections (PR #237, @gemcdaniel). * Improved compatibility with newer Jellyfin versions by updating library handling and dependency integration. * Improved library filtering to account for changes to `VirtualFolderInfo` in Jellyfin 12. * Improved recommendation behaviour and section configuration through the new per-section settings system. * Improved support for mixed-content and custom libraries across more section types. * Improved Home Screen Sections' handling of temporary user caches, including validation, expiry and automatic cleanup. * Added additional localisation keys throughout the configuration interface to make more of the plugin translatable. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed #269 where cached lazy-load pages could be accessed using a hash created for another user. Added validation, automatic cache cleanup and expiry handling for temporary user caches. * Fixed #268 where the image cache directory wasn't recreated if it was removed while Jellyfin was running. * Fixed #258 by requiring authorization for the section registration endpoint. * Fixed #247 where `/HomeScreen/Sections` could crash when Modular Home was enabled without any globally configured sections. * Fixed #242 where the scroll listener could leak and gradually cause the browser to slow down during long sessions. * Fixed #240 where duplicated file transformations could cause sections to appear multiple times and make configured upper limits, such as Because You Watched's Upper Limit, appear to be ignored. * Fixed #241 where mixed-content libraries weren't supported by the majority of sections. * Fixed #149 where Watch Again, Because You Watched and Genre could fail to return TV series or episodes because queries filtered on parameters which weren't always populated. * Fixed #226 where the Genre section didn't respect the Hide Watched setting (PR #227, @jrhigueras). * Fixed **My Requests** returning unrelated library items when a user had no requested items (PR #246, @jamesmhoward1357). * Fixed library filtering on Jellyfin 12 where `VirtualFolderInfo.ItemId` is no longer populated. * Fixed SkiaSharp dependency compatibility with the newer Jellyfin/.NET stack. * Fixed the Genre section appearing as `{0} Movies` in the admin interface. ## 🌐 Translations * Added **Norwegian Bokmål** translations (PR #239, @dyviknilsen). * Expanded and updated **Polish** translations (PR #235, @TheMatrixan). A large number of new settings, sections and localisation keys have been added in this release. As a result, **some supported languages may not yet have translations for every new string** and may temporarily fall back to English in parts of the plugin. Translation contributions are very welcome! ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The public Home Screen Sections section-registration interface remains compatible with previous releases. * `PluginInterface.RegisterSection(JObject)` is unchanged. * Existing plugins registering custom Home Screen Sections do not need to adopt a new registration payload for this release. * Home Screen Sections itself now consumes the new **Plugin Pages PluginInterface** to register its user-facing Modular Home page dynamically. * Plugins integrating with both Home Screen Sections and Plugin Pages should prefer the new programmatic Plugin Pages API rather than directly modifying Plugin Pages configuration. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**. * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier Home Screen Sections release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Updated dependencies and internal APIs to align with newer Jellyfin versions. * Home Screen Sections requires compatible releases of **File Transformation** and **Plugin Pages**. * The public Home Screen Sections `PluginInterface.RegisterSection` contract remains compatible with previous releases. ## Contributors * n00bcodr * jrhigueras * jamesmhoward1357 * gemcdaniel * dyviknilsen * TheMatrixan ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.
